Journal.Title: The New England Journal of Medicine

Article.ArticleTitle: Perioperative Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.

Abstract.AbstractText: It is uncertain whether bridging anticoagulation is necessary for patients with atrial fibrillation who need an interruption in warfarin treatment for an elective operation or other elective invasive procedure.
Forgoing bridging anticoagulation was noninferior to perioperative bridging with low-molecular-weight heparin for the prevention of arterial thromboembolism and decreased the risk of major bleeding.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparing perioperative heparin bridging strategies in mechanical heart valve patients undergoing surgery: A systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Bayesian meta-analysis of four studies comprising 1847 patients undergoing surgery with mechanical heart valves.
Bridging showed no clear thromboembolic benefit but a high probability of major bleeding harm, supporting individualized risk-adapted management over routine bridging.

Article.ArticleTitle: Direct oral anticoagulant management for neuraxial anaesthesia and deep peripheral nerve blocks.

Abstract.AbstractText: Direct oral anticoagulants increase the risk of bleeding in patients who receive neuraxial analgesia or deep peripheral nerve blocks. Clinicians must balance the risks of thromboembolic complications and spinal epidural haematoma. ASRA guidelines recommend a conservative approach with prolonged DOAC interruption and DOAC level testing in certain circumstances, whereas the PAUSE protocol offers a simplified pharmacokinetics-based strategy without routine testing.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Perioperative Anticoagulant Use for Surgery Evaluation (PAUSE) Study for Patients on a Direct Oral Anticoagulant Who Need an Elective Surgery or Procedure: Design and Rationale.

Abstract.AbstractText: Design and rationale of a prospective cohort management study establishing a standardised perioperative management plan for patients with atrial fibrillation receiving a direct oral anticoagulant who require an elective surgery or procedure.

Article.ArticleTitle: Review of article: Perioperative bridging anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation by James D. Douketis, Alex C. Spyropoulos, Scott Kaatz, et al.

Abstract.AbstractText: Commentary and critical appraisal of the BRIDGE randomized trial examining bridging anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.
